Messages.Author: Trigger
Messages.Body:
I have a couple questions on some Toreador Vampires and cards. Instead of making several posts, I'll just condense here.

1. Epikasta Rigatos - Camarilla Prince of New York: After action resolution, you can move an action card Epikasta played from your ash heap to your library (shuffle afterward).

Is this Action card during this current turn or can you pick any Action card in your Ash Heap after any action resolution? And I assume this means "Action" card, not Political action card and so on?

2.Toreador Grand Ball - Choose 2 ready Toreador you control, put this card in play and lock one of the two. The locked Toreador does not unlock as normal. The other Toreador's non-bleed actions cannot be blocked. Any minion can burn this card as a  action; Nosferatu get -1 stealth on that action.

Since this master card is not Unique, you can have two of them out at the same time, can you assign the second copy of Toreador Grand Ball's #2 ready Toreador to be the same already locked Toreador from the 1st copy of ballroom? So two Vampires can perform actions that cannot be blocked and only one 2nd vampire is tapped or do you need two separate vampires, it only does say two "Ready" Toreador vampires, not Unlocked Toreador Vampires.

3.Black Gloves - Unique melee weapon. Strike: strength+1 aggravated damage. When this weapon is used, bearer takes 1 damage during its strike resolution, but only once each combat.

Is the one damage bearer takes aggravated or normal damage?

4. Golconda: Inner Peace - Remove a vampire with capacity 8 or more from the game. His or her controller gains pool equal to the vampire's capacity. His or her controller can burn 2 pool to cancel this card as it is played.

The older version says to burn a vampire and it is not considered diablerie, Does this mean the vampire just goes to the ash heap? Is this errata to remove from the game and not to the ash heap? Can you play this on your own Vampire?

Messages.Author: Vlad
Messages.Body:
1. Any action, including political ones
2. Yes and that's the point
3. No (it's not written aggravated for the bearer)
4. No you should always refer to the latest card text. The vampire is removed from the game and of course you can play it on your own vampires.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Trigger wrote:
> I have a couple questions on some Toreador Vampires and cards. Instead of making several posts, I'll just condense here.
>
> 1. Epikasta Rigatos - Camarilla Prince of New York: After action resolution, you can move an action card Epikasta played from your ash heap to your library (shuffle afterward).
>
> Is this Action card during this current turn or can you pick any Action card in your Ash Heap after any action resolution? And I assume this means "Action" card, not Political action card and so on?
>
Only an action card Epikasta played during that action. That includes political actions card, as well as action cards played in an unusual way (for instance a .44 Magnum equipped with Concealed Weapon and destroyed during the combat).
